sources.entry: rope - Rope is a Python refactoring library.

summary.one_liner: Rope is an open source Python refactoring library, written in Python, for performing refactoring operations on Python code.
summary.what_it_does: Rope is a Python library focused on refactoring Python source code. The README describes it as light on dependencies, depending only on Python itself, and says it does not require Node.js. It states that most Python syntax up to Python 3.10 is supported. The README compares it to Jedi, saying Rope focuses on refactoring and offers more advanced refactoring operations than Jedi's basic capabilities. It links to documentation covering IDE/editor usage, configuration, a feature list, and use as a library. Since version 1.0.0 it no longer runs on Python 2; the python2 branch and 0.x.x releases are kept for that.
use_cases: rename symbols across a Python project
use refactoring in an IDE or text editor
automate Python code transformations as a library
notable: Written entirely in Python with no Node.js dependency, so it can be debugged in Python
Supports Python syntax up to Python 3.10 according to the README
Can be used from editors and IDEs or as a library
caveats: Python 2 is no longer supported since version 1.0.0; older support is only on the python2 branch or 0.x.x releases
Syntax support stops at Python 3.10 per the README; gaps are to be filed as bugs
